title: Integrate quickstart templates with Observability Pack (OTel + dashboards + local collector)
creator: Monica Patel
description:
Goal
Integrate the v1 RAG+agents quickstart templates (Python + TypeScript) with Redwood’s Observability Pack so a developer can:
1) run the template locally with traces/metrics/logs emitted via OTel,
2) use a local collector (docker-compose) for “it just works” verification,
3) optionally ship the same signals to their existing OTel backend,
4) import prebuilt dashboards + recommended alert rules (where supported).

Scope
- Ship sample OTel Collector configs (local dev + production-friendly baseline).
- Provide docker-compose.yaml for local collector + example exporter configuration.
- Ensure template code emits required spans/metrics/log fields per Redwood conventions.
- Provide “verification steps” (how to confirm traces/metrics are flowing) in template README.
- Publish/update Observability Pack assets (dashboards + alert rules) tailored to template signals.

Non-goals (v1)
- Supporting every OTel backend out-of-the-box (we’ll support: local collector + generic OTLP endpoint; add vendor-specific docs later).
- Auto-provisioning dashboards into customer Grafana/Datadog accounts.

Implementation notes
- Prefer low-cardinality attributes; avoid user_id, raw prompt text, document contents, tool arguments. Any high-card fields should be explicitly blocked/redacted at the collector.
- Logs MUST be redacted by default (API keys, auth headers, bearer tokens, PII-like fields where feasible).
- Ensure Redwood request_id correlates across logs + traces when available (dependency ENG-4189).

Acceptance criteria
1) Running `docker compose up` in the template repo starts an OTel collector that receives spans/metrics from the template app.
2) Template app emits minimum viable spans:
   - redwood.request (root)
   - redwood.llm (model call)
   - redwood.retrieval (retriever query)
   - redwood.tool (each tool execution)
   - redwood.stream (stream lifecycle, if streaming enabled)
3) Template app emits minimum viable metrics:
   - request latency (ms)
   - tokens in/out (count)
   - tool error count (count)
   - retrieval empty-result rate (count)
   - streaming disconnects (count)
4) Dashboard pack contains at least: RAG latency breakdown, tool failure rate, retrieval hit/empty rate, token economics.
5) Collector config includes redaction processors and explicit guidance on what is dropped/redacted.
6) README includes a “Verify observability” section with expected signals + troubleshooting tips (collector not receiving traces, exporter auth, port conflicts).

References / related work
- Observability Pack PRs:
  - pr-156-add-template-dashboards-rag-and-agents
  - pr-157-add-alert-rules-for-template-slos
  - pr-158-add-collector-config-examples-for-local-dev
- Quickstarts repo PRs (integration points):
  - pr-102-add-otel-instrumentation-and-log-redaction
  - pr-107-add-dockerfile-and-local-collector-compose
- Standards:
  - Confluence: Template observability standard (metrics + spans + log fields)
  - Confluence: Quickstart tracing conventions (redaction rules + span hierarchy)

Open questions
- Do we want the template to default to “collector enabled” locally, or require explicit REDWOOD_OTEL_ENABLED=1?
  - Proposed: enable by default in local dev (compose), opt-in in production templates.
- How do we tag template-originated traffic without breaking proxies that reject unknown headers?
  - Proposed: keep telemetry tag opt-in; document workaround if corporate proxy strips/blocks headers.

Rollout
- Land collector configs + compose + README verify steps in quickstarts.
- Publish dashboards/alerts in Observability Pack.
- Validate end-to-end in internal beta and update troubleshooting based on support threads.
